title: fix(sessions): report committed cleanup after publication errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session cleanup reporting that changes did not commit when lifecycle publication or owner cleanup fails after the database commit.

## User Impact

Cleanup failure reports now distinguish committed changes from rolled-back work. No schema, retention policy, or storage API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queue the existing notification on the outer transaction’s commit hook, before lifecycle publication and owner cleanup. Successful savepoints wait for the outer commit; rollback discards the notification.

## Evidence

The original producer fails three focused regression cases; the candidate passes all four, including rollback and preservation of the original error. All 30 scoped changed checks passed, and independent P2 review found no actionable issues.

The actual `runSessionsCleanup` entrypoint was also exercised with a temporary SQLite session, `fixMissing`/`enforce`, and a controlled JavaScript publication error. The row was durably deleted and the original error preserved in both runs. Only the candidate correctly reported the committed lifecycle:

```text
Original:  lifecycleCommitted=false  causePreserved=true  sessionRemoved=true
Candidate: lifecycleCommitted=true   causePreserved=true  sessionRemoved=true
```

The original failed only the commit-status assertion; the candidate passed. Both agent and shared-state async cleanup completed before fixture removal. This was a synthetic cleanup-entrypoint proof, not a production-state or native-fault test. The temporary companion was removed, all 26 bound source/dependency files remained unchanged, and the public commit did not move.
